chapter_title: The Explanation of the Peace, what it is; the Right Hand; the Kiss; the Salutation.
chapter_note: The first half is dominated by an older, systematic archetype-teaching: the five ritual signs are first located wholly within the primordial drama of the First Man (peace/right hand/kiss/salutation/laying on of hands). In the second half the register drifts strongly into ecclesial and hortatory application (church election process, offices, obedience, exhortation), consistent with editorial fatigue. Several paragraphs are mixed, pivoting from cosmic description to ‘in the midst of mankind/today’ application; one mixed paragraph also contains a likely scriptural (Ps 110:1-style) insertion.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Dialogue/Q-frame: disciples question the apostle; sets up the lesson but contains no cosmological substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: So, these five signs are the mystery of the First Man. He came forth with them from the aeon of light. Also, when he finished his contest, he went up with these good signs. They received him into the aeons of light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (“Then he says to his disciples”) as later compilation frame. Removed the ‘miniatures in the world’ explanation (“displayed in the world as miniatures…”) as cosmos→contemporary-world application.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core substrate is the impersonal, mythic claim that the five signs belong to the First Man’s descent/ascent; later editor adds framing voice and explicit ‘in the world’ application.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.38⟩ The first peace is the one that the gods and the angels in the land of light gave to the First Man; when he comes out against the enemy. The gods and the angels were walking with him; escorting him, giving to him their peace and power, and their blessing and fortification. This is the first peace that the gods and the angels gave to the First Man; as he comes forth from the aeon of light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmic-system narration (land of light; gods/angels; First Man’s sortie) without institutional address or ‘today/in the world’ anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: The first right hand is the one that the Mother of Life gave to the First Man; when he comes out to the contest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Terse, archetypal mapping (ritual sign ↔ primordial action) fully within the cosmic hierarchy.

paragraphs.core_text: The first kiss is this one with which the Mother of Life embraced the First Man; as he separates from her, coming down to the contest. Even all the gods and the angels who are in the aeons of light were making to embrace him! [ ... ] all of them also, and the church tutelaries (?), and the kinsfolk who belong to the household of his people. They were making to embrace him as [he] separates from them, accompanying him out, embracing him with the kiss of affection and love.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still functions as divine-household/aeon-of-light description; ‘church tutelaries (?)’ is lexically suspicious but remains situated in the aeons/household rather than earthly institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.39⟩ The first salutation is the salutation with which the First Man made obeisance; when he comes out [to the depths] below. He was bending his knees, making obeisance to the God of truth, and all the aeons [of light] who belong to the household of his people; entreating them for a power to escort him, as he comes forth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic obeisance and petition within the aeons; no shift to church practice or exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The first laying on of hands is the one that the Mother of Life bequeathed upon the head of the First Man. She armed him and made him mighty. She laid hands on him, and sent him to the battle. He descended. He completed his struggle with the great powers and the enmity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Archetypal action located in the primordial battle; impersonal mythic exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: By the [se] five signs and these five myst[e]ri[es] the First Man came forth from the aeons of light against the enemy. He humbled him. He was victorious against him by them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative, system-internal causality (victory ‘by’ the five mysteries) without social/institutional referents.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, when he ascended from the war, he came in to the kingdom of the household of his people by these five mysteries!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still purely cosmic geography (‘kingdom/household’) and ascent mechanics.

paragraphs.core_text: The peace with which [he ascen]ded is the peace that the summons gave to him, [w]hen it was sent forth from the [Fa]ther of Life. It gave him the peace in the world of darkness. Also, that peace with which he descended is th[e sam]e as the one with which he ascended from the struggle!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the etiological application to present practice (“Therefore… did this peace here and now come about… named and heard…”) as cosmos→contemporary-world explanation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins as cosmological mechanism (Summons from Father of Life; peace in world of darkness), then pivots to ‘here and now’ institutional/ritual justification.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this second right hand is the one that the Living Spirit gave the First Man, when he [brou]ght him upward out from the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ‘appropriate to the mystery… occurs in the midst of mankind’ application clause as a later ritual-etiology graft.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clear seam where archetype (Living Spirit saving First Man) is repurposed to explain a human custom (‘in the midst of mankind’).

paragraphs.core_text: Also, this second kiss is the one with which the [Father o]f Life and the Mother of the living embraced the First Man, when he ascended from the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the extension into human social situations (“Again, this kiss occurs among mankind…”) as application outside the cosmic system.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Archetypal embrace in the divine household is core; the explicit ‘among mankind… go away from home…’ is later social application.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.40⟩ [The] second salutation with which the First Man made obeisance [ ... this] time to the God of truth and [ ... ] the blessed aeons and al[l] the aeons [ ... the] whole [land] of light, whe[n] the Father of Life and the Mother of the living brought the Man upward from the abyss of the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ‘appropriate to the mystery… occurs today in the midst of mankind’ clause as a temporal/institutional anchoring to present practice.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is the second obeisance within the land of light; ‘occurs today’ is a strong late marker.

paragraphs.core_text: The second laying on of hands is this: When the Living Spirit brought the First Man upward from the war, he saved him from all the surging waves. He brought him upward, he gave him ease in the great aeons of light, which belong to the household of his people. He set [him] firmly before the Father, the Lord of the totality. [...] He received this great laying on of hands that he may become leader of his brethren in the new aeon.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the intervening ‘voice from the heights’ speech (“Make my son… sit at my right hand… footstool…”) as likely scriptural (Ps 110:1-style) overlay; removed the final ‘appropriate… occurs in the midst of mankind…’ institutional application.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core narrative is Living Spirit’s rescue and enthronement-before-the-Father within aeons; later hands add a biblicizing enthronement quote and then a direct mapping to human authority-giving.

paragraphs.core_text: These five mysteries and these five signs came about first in the divine. [...] these mysteries were not at the beginning amongst the powers of darkness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed ‘proclaimed in this world by an apostle… mankind has been taught… instituted them’ as hagiographic/institutional origin-claim using ‘apostle’ terminology.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The contrast ‘first in the divine… not at the beginning in darkness’ fits archaic Light-vs-darkness architecture; ‘apostle’ + ‘in this world’ proclamation is later ecclesial framing.
Cosmos→church move: Light Mind ‘comes to the world’ to ‘choose his church’; this is institutional election language rather than system-internal mapping.
Catechetical sequence (‘child of peace’, ‘elected to the faith’, approaching the church) is operational church praxis, not primordial cosmology.
Explicit obeisance to the ‘holy church’ and moral program (‘good works’) marks institutional application.
Ritual reception as ongoing community-building (‘built up in the truth for ever’) reads as pastoral consolidation, not archetypal exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again: At the time of their coming forth, the Light Form shall come forth before them; and she redeems them from the darkness to the light [ ... ] This Light Form calms the person, with the kiss and her quiet, from fear of the demons w[ho de]stroy his body. By her asp[ec]t and her image [the] heart of the elect one, who is come forth from his bo[d]y, shall be calm for [him]. Afterwards, the angel who h[o]lds the victory prize extends to him the right hand. And it draws him out of the abyss of his body, and accepts him in with the [k]iss and love. That soul shall make obeisance to its red[eem]er, who is this Light Form. And also, at the inst[ant when ... ] he shall be perfected and increased according to [ ... / ... ] in the household of the living ones, with the go[ds] and the angel[s] [...] [An]d he receives the crown [ ... ] glory in the life for ever.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional/heavenly roster tail “and all the apostles and the chosen” as cosmos→contemporary ecclesial categories (using ‘apostles’ language) appended to an otherwise mythic ascent scene.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mostly system-internal eschatological mechanics (Light Form; demons; angel; ascent from body-abyss). The insertion of ‘apostles’ as a category alongside gods/angels signals later ecclesial coloration.
Direct exhortation and audience address (‘my brethren and my limbs’; ‘let you find…’) plus self-authorization (‘Father who sent me’)—late applicatory voice.
Fragmentary but clearly oriented to hearer benefit (‘you may part from the world… you have understood…’), i.e., pastoral encouragement rather than cosmic description.
Explicit church offices (teachers/deacons/presbyters) and obedience threat (‘commits sin… against me’)—institutional discipline layer.
Imperative address (‘my beloved ones, hasten…’) and practical exhortation, with heavy lacunae; fits end-of-chapter pastoral fatigue profile.
